title: Berkeley Law bans most AI assistance in assessed work by default
friendlyTitle: Berkeley Law sets strict limits on AI for assignments and exams
summary: UC Berkeley School of Law’s Summer 2026 policy prohibits AI for conceptualizing, outlining, drafting, revising, translating or editing assessed work, and for any use in exams. Students may use it only to identify research sources unless an instructor provides a different written rule and requires disclosure.
friendlySummary: Students normally cannot use AI to plan, write, edit or translate work for marks, and cannot use it in exams. Teachers can set a different written rule, and AI may be used only to help find research sources by default.
whyItMatters: This is a concrete example of an institution separating AI fluency from the unaided skills people still need to develop. Students and employers should expect permission to become task-specific: read the rule for each course or workplace process rather than assuming a tool is either universally allowed or banned.
friendlyWhyItMatters: Schools want students to learn both legal thinking and careful AI use. The safe habit is to check the exact rule for each task before using an AI tool.
